defect.statement: In human-in-the-loop mode, the candidate_gates_passed checkpoint stores an effective obligation ledger snapshot taken before the held gates ran (spec compliance requirement verdicts and requirement closers record into the ledger after approval). Its resume fingerprint is computed from the post-gate ledger, so the checkpoint is internally inconsistent. Every resume from it sees effective_obligation_ledger CHANGED and discards the verified, human-approved candidate. The documented promise that 'a candidate is reused together with the effective obligation ledger it was verified against' (workflow.py:2603-2607) is false on the default HITL path. Fail-closed: no wrong PASS and no unbound apply, but a durability/evidence-record defect hidden by the 'resume+deferral untested' gap that this row names.

defect.statement: PRE/POST full-suite parity gap. When the host's java and mvn resolve to different JDKs and the goal states the java-side version, the candidate's gates and terminal regression run Maven under the goal JDK, while the untouched baseline (PRE) runs under the default mvn JDK. Both runs record the same environment identity, because the identity applies the goal override that the PRE execution never applied. The PRD-024 'different environments are NOT_COMPARABLE' guard is bypassed, and PRE/POST results from different JDKs are compared as the same environment. Under containment the PRE record also misstates its toolchain image (TRACED, not run: needs Docker). The main effect is false negatives (spurious CHANGED_FAILURE/NEW failures block correct candidates) plus a baseline record whose environment provenance is wrong (rule 14 evidence binding). A PRE failure excusing a POST failure is theoretically possible only with equal normalized fingerprints across JDKs, which I judge unlikely (INFERRED).
